effects: Pulls exactly `assets` USDC from the signer into the vault (enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
Mints vault shares (humaUSDC) to `onBehalf`. The number is previewDeposit(assets), set by the vault's share price at execution, with no minimum.
formats.shown: Deposit 1 USDC for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker humaUSDC and the share recipient shown as fields.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted is not shown and has no on-chain minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The price comes from storage (totalAssets, totalSupply, fees). Case 0: the signer received 1e18 humaUSDC and the screen shows only the ticker. The reader wrote 'amount not shown'.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds it. A wallet could only estimate it with previewDeposit.

findings.title: deposit: 'Share ticker' is a standalone raw constant field and says nothing about an amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'} renders 'humaUSDC' on its own line.
findings.fix: Fold it into the wording, e.g. intent 'Deposit USDC for humaUSDC shares', or label 'You receive: humaUSDC shares'.

cases.notes: The 1 USDC out is shown exactly. The humaUSDC shares in are shown by ticker and recipient, but the 1e18 amount is not shown (it is computed on-chain).

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns vault shares from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up at the current share price.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, it spends that many shares from onBehalf's allowance to the signer.
Sends exactly `assets` USDC from the vault to `receiver`, pulling liquidity from the liquidity adapter when idle funds are short.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 620000 USDC to <receiver>, with Owner <onBehalf>.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of humaUSDC shares burned from the owner is not shown and has no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`, then exit(): `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 1: 619503.62 humaUSDC left the signer and the screen shows no share amount. The reader wrote 'amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Not in calldata. A wallet could only estimate it with previewWithdraw.

cases.notes: The 620000 USDC in to the receiver is shown exactly. The burn of 619503.6 humaUSDC is implied by 'Owner', but no amount is shown.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` humaUSDC from `onBehalf`, spending the signer's allowance when the signer is not onBehalf.
Sends previewRedeem(shares) USDC to `receiver`. The amount is set by the share price at execution, with no minimum.
formats.shown: Redeem 5 humaUSDC to <receiver>, with Owner <onBehalf>. The asset paid out is never named.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount paid out is not shown and has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`, which ends in `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets)`. Case 2: the signer received 4.999999 USDC, a number that is not on the screen.
findings.fix: Not in calldata. A wallet could only estimate it with previewRedeem.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says the payout is USDC. The reader was unsure what asset arrives.
findings.evidence: descriptor redeem interpolatedIntent 'Redeem {#.shares} to {#.receiver}' has no field naming the underlying asset, although metadata.constants.underlyingTicker='USDC' exists. Case 2 reader: 'Whether the payout is USDC; screen only says redeem shares'.
findings.fix: Use interpolatedIntent 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}', or add a field such as {label:'Receive asset', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'}.

cases.notes: The 5 humaUSDC out is shown exactly. The 4.999999 USDC in is not shown, either as an asset or as an amount. The reader guessed USDC but was unsure.
